# Colecto v0.7.1

Automatic labels work on a real Inbox, a calmer reader that uses your screen, zoom in the
desktop app, and settings that your MCP tools can change for you.

## What you'll notice

- **Automatic labels and "Check mail again" work.** With real mail in your Inbox, the AI
  extension asked for more than it could receive at once, so **Check mail again** said
  "The AI extension did not answer" and new mail was not labelled. It now reads one
  message at a time.
- **Wider messages.** The message body uses much more of the reader's width instead of a
  narrow column.
- **Conversations that stay out of the way.** Earlier and later messages of a
  conversation now sit behind a small **Show 1 earlier message** control, one line each,
  and open in place when you click them. The message you opened stays in view.
- **Clearer label rules.** In **Settings → AI**, each label is a row with **Edit** and
  **Remove** buttons. The rule editor's fields line up, and it says that each rule is a
  regular expression, so `^order #\d+` works as well as plain words. See
  [AI features](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.7.1/docs/ai.md).
- **Zoom.** In the desktop app, **Ctrl +** and **Ctrl −** zoom the whole interface and
  **Ctrl 0** resets it. The level is remembered. In a browser, its own zoom keeps working.
- **Settings over MCP.** API keys can be allowed to read and change appearance,
  notification and extension settings, each area granted separately and all off by
  default. Credentials, connections, keys and extensions stay yours alone. See
  [Self-hosting](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.7.1/docs/self-hosting.md).
- **Fixes.** The scrollbar no longer shows through a dialog opened over Settings. Menus
  and the welcome screen no longer use blur effects, which made animations stutter on
  Linux.
